Basic concept

The basic idea is to inject a patient with lipid-encapsulated, chemically modified mRNA to dodge the immune system and allow the uptake of the particles into the patient's cells upon which the mRNA is translated into a protein. Depending on the protein this concept can be used for three different applications (see "The three different applications of the protein").

Lipid-capsule

The lipid-capsule from what I understand serves primarily as the delivery system into the cell as well as limiting the premature degradation of the mRNA.

Chemically modified mRNA

The chemical modification of the mRNA allows it to "dodge" the immune system. From what I read uridine is replaced with a pseudouridine. The shape of the "modified uridine" then prevents it from locking into and activating receptors that detect foreign RNA.

mRNA assembled using a pseudouridine greatly reduced the tendency of immune sentinels called dendritic cells to shoot out inflammatory molecules in response.

A way to tame the cells' typical inflammatory response is to modify one of the mRNA's four building blocks, uridine. For example mRNA assembled with 1-methylpseudouridine bore a chemical "bump" that the team suspected kept it from locking into key receptors on the surface of immune cells.

The three different applications of the protein:

Use as a drug:

"Mice recovering from induced heart attacks survived longer and had stronger hearts when injected with mRNA encoding a protein that drives blood vessel formation—vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)."

Passive Immunization:

Rather than injecting the patient with antibodies extracted from a cured patient who suffered from the same disease or "lab-made" antibodies, the mRNA encodes a monoclonal antibody which is then produced by the patient itself.

"Intravenous injection of a lipid nanoparticle–encapsulated mRNA molecule encoding this antibody protected mice against viral infection and virus-associated arthritis and also induced protective concentrations of serum antibody in macaques."

Classic passive immunization however does not make the patient immune to the infection itself since your own immune system was not trained to produce the antibodies itself. Active Immunization
